Title: Document 12
Content: Richard Aldington, junior officer, Life for Life's Sake, memoir, published `text(1941)`.

I realized that the London I had come back to was a different place from the London I had left in `text(1914)`, let alone prewar London. Everything seemed askew...London was crowded with enormous numbers of “war workers,” who still clung to their jobs like limpets. There was a devil-take-the-hindmost scramble for money and position in the new world, and an extravagance which seemed incredible to `text(one)` who had known the old sober England. I stood aghast at this degeneration of my people, visible to me, as it was not to them, because of my long absence. I asked myself anxiously if I too had not degenerated, and it seemed to me I had.
